events.title: Emperor Claudius Dies and Nero Takes the Throne
events.description: Roman emperor Claudius died in mysterious circumstances, widely believed to be poisoning. His adopted son Nero was named successor instead of Claudius's own son Britannicus.
events.significance: Nero's rise began one of the most infamous reigns in Roman history and ended the Julio-Claudian line in turmoil.

events.title: Knights Templar Arrested in France
events.description: At dawn, King Philip IV of France ordered the arrest of hundreds of Knights Templar across his kingdom. Many later confessed to heresy under torture.
events.significance: The arrests began the downfall of the powerful medieval military order, which was dissolved a few years later. Friday the 13th superstitions are often linked to the event.

events.title: Italy Declares War on Germany
events.description: Italy's new government, which had broken with Mussolini's regime, sided with the Allies and declared war on its former partner, Germany.
events.significance: The declaration formalized Italy's switch of sides in World War II and set the stage for a hard campaign up the Italian peninsula.

events.title: Uruguayan Air Force Flight 571 Crashes in the Andes
events.description: A plane carrying a Uruguayan rugby team and others crashed in the Andes mountains. Twenty-eight people survived the impact, but all but 16 died before rescue on December 23.
events.significance: The survivors' ordeal became one of history's best-known survival stories and drew worldwide attention.
